summary: Master has not made this moot: kernel_fn still runs FusedQKNorm, the k/v FP8 casts, store_cache and the q FP8 cast as separate launches, and the change is a strict superset of the neutral cache-store-fused-fp8-cast because it also folds FusedQKNorm. The gain it can show is small, about 2-3% on the batch-1 shapes and +0.5-0.8% on the headline, inside the CI, so read it on the decode_1 and verify_1 rows. The spec predates head pairing, so the implementer has to say what the paired branch does with the new FP8 q.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. At T=1 and T=8 the layer is a serial chain of latency-bound launches inside a CUDA graph. The 172.8/182.1 us decode_1 and 238/248 us verify_1 shapes sit 4x above their floors (40-66 us), and launch overhead is a large part of that gap. The sibling measured 3.5-6.4 us for this same 5->1 fusion. If those microseconds carry over unchanged to the serialized layer graph (no overlap hides them on the main stream before FA3), the claimed ~2-3.5% on decode_1 and ~1.5-2.5% on verify_1 follows. The expected directions match TASK.md. decode_1 and verify_1 are where a few us matter, and every batch-16/32 shape is 260-1070 us and Marlin/FA3 dominated, so flat is the right call there. Geomean arithmetic: two of six loads gaining ~2-3% gives about +0.5-0.8% on the headline, which is inside the ±1.5% CI. The run is therefore only readable per shape, or from the profile: the replaced kernels' rows (FusedQKNorm Triton, the unrolled_elementwise casts, store_cache, the q cast) should disappear and one ~2-3 us Triton row should appear. Weakest link: LESSONS records that tiny-kernel fusions were flat on decode_layer shapes. In particular cache-store-fused-fp8-cast, which removed 3 of these 4 cast/store launches, came back within noise (1.011/1.009 on decode_1). So the case rests almost entirely on FusedQKNorm (plus the last q cast) being worth ~2-4 us on its own in this layer. The sibling's savings were measured on 17-36 us attention-only shapes, where L2 state and PDL overlap differ. In the full layer the attention input comes from the qkv GEMM, and only qkv is warm, not the whole working set. Expect the low end of 3.5-6.4 us, and a decode_1 result anywhere from flat to +3%.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: on full layers with batch>1 (full decode_16/32, verify_16/32), master builds q_attn with torch.zeros plus two strided copies from the bf16 q, and that copy also does the BF16->E4M3 cast. With the spec as written, the fused kernel emits an unpadded FP8 q [T,16,64], and the pad path stays as zeros plus two copies (now FP8->FP8). On those shapes the saving is therefore only FusedQKNorm, the k/v casts and the store. The pad launches stay, so they read flat, which agrees with the spec's 'flat'. Batch-1 shapes are never paired, so the decode_1 and verify_1 rows that carry the hypothesis are not confounded. If the implementer instead ports the sibling's current PAIRED branch (padded q written straight from the kernel), the paired shapes would also lose the zeros and copy launches. That is a separate sub-change and should not be folded in silently, because it would mix two effects on the full batch>1 rows.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: it touches only the router and the boundary kernel's router_dtype at T=8, downstream of attention. No interaction with the pre-attention chain. Its FusedQKNorm/cos_sin table is the very thing being replaced, and the spec reads the same table, so RoPE numerics stay aligned with it.
marlin-block-m-cap-16: it affects only the MoE GEMMs at T>=32. No interaction.
interference: No companion is warranted. The predicted gain sits on the batch-1 shapes, which no landed hypothesis touches in the pre-attention path. Pairing applies only at batch>1 and the router change is downstream. A gain or a loss on decode_1/verify_1 can be attributed to the fusion directly, and the profile's replaced-kernel rows confirm it independently of drift. An ab-revert of head pairing would only change the full batch>1 shapes, which are predicted flat, so it cannot disambiguate anything. A control splitting FusedQKNorm from the cast/store fusion is already effectively on file: cache-store-fused-fp8-cast measured the cast/store part (flat), so this run's delta over it is the FusedQKNorm fold. The real ambiguity is drift: ~2% effects against 1.5-2.5% per-shape drift. Settle that with the profile's kernel times rather than a second run.
rules_flags: None blocking. q goes fp32 -> FP8 E4M3 directly, and k and v go fp32 -> (divided by scale) -> FP8. That is allowed: queries may be rounded to FP8 and the cache stays FP8. It is no coarser than master's fp32 -> bf16 -> FP8, and the cache-entry error stays well within 8%.

The cos_sin table was built in prepare() from constants, not from data, and the kernel indexes it by positions[t] on the device. The table has 2^21 rows, which covers the 1,048,576+8 context test. No caching derived from inputs.

The kv_scale branch must stay on cfg['kv_scale'] or be unconditional (dividing by the loaded scale, which is exact at 1.0). Never branch on k_scale's value. The kernel must load k_scale/v_scale through pointers, never with .item().

In-place writes into k_cache/v_cache through view(-1, 128) rely on contiguity. Add a shape/stride assert in Python (host-side, on metadata only, graph-safe) so that page-64 or non-contiguous caches cannot silently misaddress. The sibling's reviewer asked for the same hardening (DECISIONS 2026-10-24).
Every row in cache_loc is written, matching master's reserved_skip_index=-1. Slot 0 is live here.
open_questions: Paired branch: the spec says the FP8 q goes to FA3 'unchanged otherwise', but it was written before head pairing landed. Confirm that the implementation feeds the kernel's FP8 q [T,16,64] into master's existing zeros-plus-two-copies pad on the paired path, and does not adopt the sibling's PAIRED in-kernel write. The PAIRED write is the obvious follow-up hypothesis (depends_on this one) for full batch>1 shapes, where it removes two or three more launches; attention_decode got 1.244x from it.

Exactly which launches disappear at T=1 depends on whether k/v are divided (only when kv_scale != 1) and on whether q.view().to(FP8) is still a separate launch on the unpaired path. Count the removed kernel rows in the decode_1 profile so the measured us per removed launch can go into LESSONS whatever the outcome.

Does FusedQKNorm's RoPE use the same interleaved pairing (2i, 2i+1) and the table layout cos[0:32] | sin[32:64] indexed by pair i? The spec assumes so from prepare(). A mismatch would show up only on sliding layers (rope_theta set) and should fail the sliding tests loudly rather than subtly. Verify it against sglang's fused_qk_norm source before submitting.
num_warps=1 with grid (T, 18) is fine at T<=8. At T=256 (verify_32) it is 4,608 tiny programs. Still cheap, but check that the verify_32 row does not regress against the separate vectorized casts.
